messages.text:
The first read confirmed this is a Clap single-command CLI with brute-force, dictionary, and mask modes, but the combined source dump was truncated.

I’m narrowing now to the contract boundaries that affect observable parity: argument parsing messages, candidate generation order, ZIP test semantics, and entrypoint shape.

rust-reference/README.md:1:# zip-password-finder
rust-reference/README.md:2:[![Build](https://github.com/agourlay/zip-password-finder/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/agourlay/zip-password-finder/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
rust-reference/README.md:3:[![Crates.io](https://img.shields.io/crates/v/zip-password-finder.svg)](https://crates.io/crates/zip-password-finder)
rust-reference/README.md:5:`zip-password-finder` is a tool to find the password of protected zip files.
rust-reference/README.md:13:- Supports both ZipCrypto and AES encryption
rust-reference/README.md:15:- Three attack modes: brute force, dictionary, and mask attack
rust-reference/README.md:16:- Graceful interruption with Ctrl-C, displaying the last password tested
rust-reference/README.md:17:- Resume brute force from a specific password with `--startingPassword`
rust-reference/README.md:25:Generates all passwords for a given charset and password length range. This is the default mode when no dictionary or mask is provided.
rust-reference/README.md:28:zip-password-finder -i archive.zip -c lud --minPasswordLen 1 --maxPasswordLen 6
rust-reference/README.md:31:The available charset presets are:
rust-reference/README.md:44:Alternatively, a custom charset file can be provided with `--charsetFile`. It should be a text file containing a single line of characters to use for the generation.
rust-reference/README.md:46:To resume an interrupted brute force search, use `--startingPassword` to skip ahead:
rust-reference/README.md:49:zip-password-finder -i archive.zip --startingPassword "abc"
rust-reference/README.md:54:Tests passwords from a text file, one word per line.
rust-reference/README.md:57:zip-password-finder -i archive.zip -p wordlist.txt
rust-reference/README.md:62:Generates passwords matching a pattern where each position has its own charset. This is useful when you know part of the password structure (e.g. starts with uppercase, ends with digits).
rust-reference/README.md:65:zip-password-finder -i archive.zip --mask '?u?l?l?l?d?d'
rust-reference/README.md:68:The available mask tokens are:
rust-reference/README.md:78:  ?1 | custom charset 1 (--customCharset1)
rust-reference/README.md:79:  ?2 | custom charset 2 (--customCharset2)
rust-reference/README.md:80:  ?3 | custom charset 3 (--customCharset3)
rust-reference/README.md:81:  ?4 | custom charset 4 (--customCharset4)
rust-reference/README.md:85:Any other character in the mask is treated as a literal.
rust-reference/README.md:87:Custom charsets are defined with `--customCharset1` through `--customCharset4` and can contain literal characters and/or built-in tokens. For example, `--customCharset1 "aeiou"` defines vowels, and `--customCharset1 "?l?d"` defines lowercase letters + digits.
rust-reference/README.md:93:zip-password-finder -i archive.zip --mask '?l?l?l?d?d'
rust-reference/README.md:96:zip-password-finder -i archive.zip --mask 'pass?d?d?d?d'
rust-reference/README.md:99:zip-password-finder -i archive.zip --mask '?u?l?l?l?l?s'
rust-reference/README.md:101:# custom charset: 2 vowels followed by a digit
rust-reference/README.md:102:zip-password-finder -i archive.zip -1 "aeiou" --mask '?1?1?d'
rust-reference/README.md:109:Using the provided binaries in https://github.com/agourlay/zip-password-finder/releases
rust-reference/README.md:113:Using Cargo via [crates.io](https://crates.io/crates/zip-password-finder).
rust-reference/README.md:116:cargo install zip-password-finder
rust-reference/README.md:121:You can install [`zip-password-finder`](https://aur.archlinux.org/packages?O=0&K=zip-password-finder) from the AUR using an [AUR helper](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/AUR_helpers). For example:

rust-reference/README.md:131:Find the password of protected ZIP files
rust-reference/README.md:133:Usage: zip-password-finder [OPTIONS] --inputFile <inputFile>
rust-reference/README.md:137:  -w, --workers <workers>                        number of workers
rust-reference/README.md:138:  -p, --passwordDictionary <passwordDictionary>  path to a password dictionary file
rust-reference/README.md:139:  -c, --charset <charset>                        charset to use to generate password [default: lud]
rust-reference/README.md:140:      --charsetFile <charsetFile>                path to a charset file
rust-reference/README.md:141:      --minPasswordLen <minPasswordLen>          minimum password length [default: 1]
rust-reference/README.md:142:      --maxPasswordLen <maxPasswordLen>          maximum password length [default: 10]
rust-reference/README.md:143:      --fileNumber <fileNumber>                  file number in the zip archive [default: 0]
rust-reference/README.md:144:  -s, --startingPassword <startingPassword>      password to start from
rust-reference/README.md:145:  -m, --mask <mask>                              mask pattern for mask attack (e.g. '?l?l?l?d?d')
rust-reference/README.md:146:  -1, --customCharset1 <customCharset1>          custom charset 1 for mask attack, referenced as ?1
rust-reference/README.md:147:  -2, --customCharset2 <customCharset2>          custom charset 2 for mask attack, referenced as ?2
rust-reference/README.md:148:  -3, --customCharset3 <customCharset3>          custom charset 3 for mask attack, referenced as ?3
rust-reference/README.md:149:  -4, --customCharset4 <customCharset4>          custom charset 4 for mask attack, referenced as ?4
rust-reference/README.md:156:For AES make sure to use a CPU with `SHA` instructions (Intel Sandy Bridge or newer, AMD Bulldozer or newer) to get the best performance.
